title: OKR Alignment Almanac: cross-team commitments, cadence, and escalation
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Goal: Create an operational playbook (the 'Almanac') that standardizes how company-level OKRs are translated into cross-functional initiatives, how teams commit to work each cycle, and how escalations and trade-offs are handled so execution is predictable.

Problem: We have recurring friction at the boundary between company objectives and team roadmaps: handoffs are inconsistent, commit expectations vary by team, and risks are surfaced too late. This causes slippage on high-visibility initiatives (runtime optimizations, Dedicated capacity SLAs, Private deployment certifications) and creates repeated ad-hoc escalation overhead.

Scope: The Almanac covers:
- A commitment cadence (quarterly + mid-cycle recon) with templated artifacts for PMs and Eng leads.
- A commitment ledger format: initiative owner, expected outcomes, acceptance criteria, risk lanes, and rollback/fallback policies.
- A cross-team dependency registry and lightweight gating rules for canary/rollout decisions (ties into Console/rollouts tooling).
- An escalation window and SLA for resolving cross-team blockers during each cycle.
- A minimal set of metrics for measuring alignment success (commit accuracy, blocked lead time, objective coverage).

Deliverables:
1) OKR Alignment Almanac doc (Confluence) with templates and examples mapped to Redwood product pillars (runtime, Console, Dedicated, Private).
2) A Miro template for running the quarter planning workshop (roles, DACI, and risk lanes).
3) A lightweight GH PR/checklist template for initiative gating that links to rollout policies and dashboards.

Success criteria:
- 80% of company-level initiatives have an approved commitment ledger before cycle start.
- Median time-to-resolve cross-team blockers reduces by 40% within two cycles.
- Adoption: >= 70% of PMs report the Almanac reduced ambiguity in the quarter planning survey.
acceptance_criteria: Almanac document published in Confluence with templates and at least three mapped examples (runtime, Dedicated, Private).
Cadence playbook (quarterly planning + mid-cycle recon) reviewed and signed off by GTM, Eng, Design, Research leads.
Dependency registry format trialed in one cross-functional initiative and used to unblock at least one critical dependency.
Oncall escalation windows and RACI defined and integrated into the existing incident/escalation runbook.
decisions: Use a lightweight ledger (single Confluence page per initiative) rather than a heavy PM tool integration to prioritize speed and visibility.
Standardize on three risk lanes (technical, resourcing, external) and require mitigation notes for any 'high' risk.
Require an explicit rollback/fallback policy for any initiative that touches runtime or Dedicated capacity.
tradeoffs: Simplicity vs. fidelity: the ledger intentionally captures high-level trade decisions and links to deeper artifacts (PRDs, RFCs) rather than duplicating information.
Speed vs. enforcement: adoption is driven by playbook clarity and leader buy-in rather than automated gating to avoid blocking ship schedules.
